hints: Focus on whether the catalyst in each familiar industrial process is a pure transition metal or a metal combined with another element.
Recall the Contact process catalyst for oxidising $\text{SO}_2$ to $\text{SO}_3$, it is orange vanadium(V) oxide, $\text{V}_2\text{O}_5$.
Now check the other three processes and notice they all use pure metals like Pt, Fe and Ni, so pick the one that stands out as a compound.
walkthrough:
**Sort elements from compounds**

Think like a teacher with you. An element catalyst is just a pure metal, like Fe or Ni. A compound catalyst is a metal joined to a non-metal, like an oxide.

Key idea:
$$\text{element} = \text{pure metal, compound} = \text{metal + non-metal}$$

**List the four famous catalysts**

Let us recall each one together. This is pure memory work for Paper 1.

$$\text{catalytic converters: Pt, Pd, Rh (elements)}$$ 
$$\text{Contact process: V}_2\text{O}_5 \text{ (compound)}$$ 
$$\text{Haber process: Fe (element)}$$ 
$$\text{hydrogenation: Ni (element)}$$

**Pick the odd one out**

Only the Contact process uses vanadium(V) oxide to oxidise sulfur dioxide:
$$2\text{SO}_2 + \text{O}_2 \rightleftharpoons 2\text{SO}_3$$
The other three all use pure transition metal elements, so the compound catalyst is the Contact process.

options.A: Incorrect. Catalytic converters use the elements platinum, palladium and rhodium as a thin coating. These are pure transition metals, not compounds.
options.B: Correct. The Contact process for making sulfuric acid uses vanadium(V) oxide, $\text{V}_2\text{O}_5$, which is clearly a compound of vanadium and oxygen, to catalyse $2\text{SO}_2 + \text{O}_2 \rightleftharpoons 2\text{SO}_3$.
options.C: Incorrect. The Haber process for ammonia uses finely divided iron, Fe, with promoters. Iron here is used as the pure element, not a compound.
options.D: Incorrect. Hydrogenation of alkenes uses nickel, Ni (or Pt/Pd), as a heterogeneous catalyst. This is the pure metal element, not a compound.
